historical_references.reference: The Nabis were a group of priest-kings who ruled the Achaemenid Empire in Persia during the late 5th and early 4th centuries BCE. They are known to have held power in Persepolis and other major cities, and their reign marked a period of religious and political instability in the empire.

The Nabis were also a dynasty of Hindu rulers in ancient India, particularly in the southern regions. They are believed to have ruled during the late 2nd millennium BCE, and their reign coincided with the decline of the Harappan Civilization.
